rounds.scope: math — Kaiming/Xavier derivations, Xiong Pre/Post-LN scalings, DeepNorm, GPT-2 1/√(2N), residual Jacobian
rounds.confirmed_correct: Var(z)=n_in·Var(W)·E[x^2]; E[ReLU(z)^2]=½Var(z) → Kaiming Var(W)=2/n_in; Xavier 2/(n_in+n_out); Xiong Post-LN top-grad Θ(d√ln d) depth-independent vs Pre-LN O(d√(ln d/L)) decaying; DeepNorm α=(2N)^{1/4}, β=(8N)^{-1/4}; GPT-2 1/√(2N) (2 residual writes/layer); residual Jacobian ∏(I+∂F/∂x) identity term; Pre-LN residual-stream std ∝√l. Crucially confirmed the SECOND-MOMENT subtlety (see code round): post-ReLU E[y^2]≈1 preserved, but Var(y)=1-1/π≈0.68 because ReLU mean≠0 — the propagated quantity is E[y^2], not Var.

real_issues_caught: METHODOLOGICAL CONFOUND in [d] (Pre-LN vs Post-LN gradient): the original demo measured ||dL/dx|| with loss=mean(stack(x)^2), but a Post-LN stack's output is LayerNorm-normalized so that loss is ~scale-invariant and artificially suppresses ALL gradients → the headline '4.3e6× more gradient' was largely an artifact of output-normalization asymmetry, not pure Post-LN gradient pathology. VERIFIED on Server5 via a probe: with a symmetric final-LN+head, the ||dL/dx|| ratio collapses to 1.2×. FIX: redesigned [d] to measure the per-block weight-grad TOP/BOTTOM ratio (last/first) with a final linear head — a metric robust to the loss choice (Xiong's actual claim). New result: Pre-LN=0.40 (balanced), Post-LN=2.35 (top-heavy, >1). Re-ran clean on Server5.
rounds.confirmed_correct: [a] LayerNorm==nn.LayerNorm (pop var, eps in sqrt); [b] RMSNorm==nn.RMSNorm + mean-shift-variance (LN invariant 9.5e-7, RMS not 3.05); [c] BatchNorm train≠eval; [e] Kaiming E[y^2]=1.00 / Xavier 0.50 (measuring SECOND MOMENT not Var — corrected from the subagent's '.var()≈1' which is actually 0.68); [f] residual var unscaled ×51 vs 1/√(2N) ×1.5. All 6 asserts pass on Server5 (torch 2.10).
